Three-panel academic concept figure for a TOP venue paper (EMNLP 2026). Full width (figure*), aspect ratio ~3.5:1, figsize (14, 4) inches.

OVERALL LAYOUT:
Three large rounded-corner panels side by side with equal spacing. Each panel is a rounded rectangle (corner radius 12px) with a distinct background color forming a warm-to-cold gradient left to right. Panels have subtle drop shadow (2px offset, 8% opacity). Thin gray border (#E0E0E0, 0.5pt) on each panel.

Panel widths: (a) ~35%, (b) ~30%, (c) ~35%
Vertical padding inside panels: generous (at least 8% top/bottom)
Horizontal gap between panels: ~2% of total width

---

PANEL (a) — LEFT — "Small Panel (K=3)"
Background: warm peach (#FFEBEE, Material Red 50)
Panel label: "(a)" in 12pt bold serif (Times) at top-left corner inside panel
Panel title: "Individual Vulnerability Dominates" in 9pt bold serif, centered below panel label

Content (top to bottom):
1. THREE circular judge icons arranged in a triangle (equilateral, pointing up):
   - Top-left icon: medium blue circle (#5C6BC0, Indigo 400) with thin white border (1.5pt), diameter ~0.6 inches. Text label "Judge 1" in 7pt sans-serif next to it.
   - Top-right icon: medium blue circle (#5C6BC0) same style. Text label "Judge 2" in 7pt sans-serif next to it.
   - Bottom-center icon: RED circle (#E53935, Red 600) with a small white "!" icon inside — this is the vulnerable judge. Text label "Compromised" in 7pt bold red sans-serif below it, or "Manipulated" as a red annotation.

2. Below the judges: a CHAIN LINK illustration (3 interlocking oval links), oriented horizontally, centered:
   - Two links in muted gray (#90A4AE)
   - One link in RED (#E53935) — the weak link, slightly cracked/broken visual
   - Below the chain: text "Weakest link determines outcome" in 7pt italic serif, centered, color #757575

3. At the bottom of the panel: a horizontal stacked bar (width ~80% of panel, height ~10px):
   - LEFT portion: RED (#E53935) taking ~70% of bar width, labeled "η_max dominates" in 7pt below-left
   - RIGHT portion: BLUE (#1565C0) taking ~30% of bar width, labeled "K_eff minor" in 7pt below-right

4. Bottom-left corner: "K = 3" in 10pt serif, muted gray (#757575)

---

PANEL (b) — CENTER — "Transition Zone"
Background: light warm yellow (#FFF8E1, Material Amber 50)
Panel label: "(b)" in 12pt bold serif at top-left corner
Panel title: "η_max Diminishes with Panel Size" in 9pt bold serif, centered below panel label

Content:
1. A BALANCE / SEESAW visualization centered in the panel:
   - A triangular fulcrum (gray #9E9E9E) in the center
   - A horizontal beam (dark gray #616161, 2pt thick) resting on the fulcrum
   - LEFT side of beam: a RED dot (#E53935, ~0.3 inches) with text label "η_max" in 8pt red italic below the dot, and subscript "(individual)" in 6pt gray below that
   - RIGHT side of beam: a BLUE dot (#1565C0, ~0.3 inches) with text label "K_eff" in 8pt blue italic below the dot, and subscript "(collective)" in 6pt gray below that
   - The beam should be nearly level but tilted ~5-8 degrees (left side slightly lower, meaning η_max still slightly heavier at transition)

2. Above the seesaw: a curved arrow (#78909C, 1pt) arcing from left to right, with text "As K increases →" in 8pt sans-serif above the arrow

3. Below the seesaw: a horizontal GRADIENT BAR (not split — smooth gradient from RED #E53935 on left to BLUE #1565C0 on right):
   - Width ~80% of panel, height ~8px, rounded ends
   - Left end labeled "K=3" in 7pt gray
   - Right end labeled "K≥5" in 7pt gray
   - This replaces the old X-shaped crossover bars — much simpler and clearer

---

PANEL (c) — RIGHT — "Large Panel (K≥5)"
Background: light blue (#E3F2FD, Material Blue 50)
Panel label: "(c)" in 12pt bold serif at top-left corner
Panel title: "Collective Diversity Absorbs Manipulation" in 9pt bold serif, centered below panel label

Content (top to bottom):
1. SEVEN circular judge icons arranged in a hexagonal network layout (one center + six surrounding):
   - All circles in various SHADES OF BLUE (ranging from #1565C0 dark to #90CAF9 light) — representing diversity
   - Diameter ~0.45 inches each, thin white borders (1.5pt)
   - THIN GRAY LINES (#B0BEC5, 0.5pt) connecting adjacent nodes (network graph mesh, not fully connected — show ~12 edges for readability)
   - Text annotation "Diverse judges" in 8pt sans-serif above the network, centered
   - One or two edges labeled "pairwise independence" in 6pt gray italic (using a small annotation arrow pointing to a representative edge)
   - No red nodes — all judges are reasonably robust in diverse panels

2. Below the network: a horizontal stacked bar (same style as panel a):
   - LEFT portion: BLUE (#1565C0) taking ~75% of bar, labeled "K_eff dominates" in 7pt below-left
   - RIGHT portion: very faint RED (#FFCDD2) taking ~25%, labeled "η_max minor" in 7pt below-right

3. Bottom-right corner: "K ≥ 5" in 10pt serif, muted gray (#757575)

---

BOTTOM LEGEND STRIP (below all three panels):
A single-line legend strip centered below:
- Small red circle + "η_max (weakest-link vulnerability)" in 8pt
- Small blue circle + "K_eff (MI-based diversity score)" in 8pt
- Small gradient bar icon + "Relative predictive weight" in 7pt italic gray

---

STYLE REQUIREMENTS:
- Publication quality for a TOP venue (EMNLP 2026)
- Elegant, premium, sophisticated — NOT cheap or homework-like
- Subtle drop shadows (2px, 10% opacity) on panel boxes
- Rounded corners (12px) on panel rectangles
- Thin, elegant elements — not bulky matplotlib defaults
- Serif font (Times New Roman) for panel labels, panel titles, and K annotations
- Sans-serif (Helvetica/DejaVu Sans) for annotation labels and legend
- Muted, harmonious color palette — warm-to-cold semantic gradient
- Generous white space between and within panels
- Consistent visual weight across all three panels
- 300 DPI, white outer background
- NO matplotlib default styling: NO gray figure background, NO thick gridlines, NO tab10 colors
- NO text mentioning "shift" or "crossover"
- All text must be readable at column width (minimum 7pt when scaled down to single column)
- TEXT LABELS ARE CRITICAL: every visual element should have a clear text annotation so a new reader can understand the figure without reading the caption
